# Ramune — Full Documentation

Foundation for Workers-style platforms in Go, embeddable and extensible; Cloudflare-Workers-compatible out of the box. Primary use case: build your own Workers-style platform (your `env`, your backends, your bindings) on a runtime that already speaks the Workers handler shape, so Cloudflare-authored handlers (`export default { fetch(req, env, ctx), scheduled }`) run unchanged as a consequence of the default surface. Deploy to your own hardware with full Go interop. Core scope: [WinterCG](https://wintercg.org/) + fetch + `env.DB` / `env.KV` / `env.SECRETS` + `ctx.waitUntil` + cron. Advanced CF bindings (Durable Objects / Queues / R2 / AI Gateway) are **not shipped**; they are implemented as user-supplied `env.*` bindings via `RegisterFunc` + `WithExtraEnvJS`, and the same mechanism is how you design bindings that have no CF analogue at all. **No Cgo**: JSC via `purego`, QuickJS pure Go; `go build` cross-compiles to any GOOS/GOARCH without a C toolchain, and QuickJS runs on `FROM scratch` Docker. Ramune is also a complete JS/TS runtime (`run` / `test` / `check` / `fmt` / `lint` / `repl` / `compile`) and an embeddable JS engine for any Go program.

> Ramune is a JavaScript/TypeScript runtime and embeddable JS engine for Go. Dual backend: JavaScriptCore (JIT, macOS/Linux) via [purego](https://github.com/ebitengine/purego) and QuickJS (pure Go, cross-platform incl. Windows) via [modernc.org/quickjs](https://pkg.go.dev/modernc.org/quickjs) — no Cgo required for either.

## Install

```
# JSC backend (default, macOS/Linux)
go install github.com/i2y/ramune/cmd/ramune@latest
go install github.com/i2y/ramune/cmd/ramune-toolchain@latest  # needed for check / fmt / lint / compile / transpile / typegen
ramune setup-jit   # macOS only: enable JSC JIT for full performance

# QuickJS backend (Windows / zero-dependency)
go install -tags quickjs github.com/i2y/ramune/cmd/ramune@latest
go install -tags quickjs github.com/i2y/ramune/cmd/ramune-toolchain@latest  # optional

# Smaller binary
go install -tags nosqlite -ldflags="-s -w" github.com/i2y/ramune/cmd/ramune@latest
```

The `ramune` binary (~30MB) holds the runtime. `ramune-toolchain` (~60MB) is a separate dev-only binary that `ramune` exec-dispatches to for `check` / `fmt` / `lint` / `compile` / `transpile` / `typegen`. Splitting the tsgo + rslint + gotranspiler trees out of the main binary keeps `ramune run` / `serve` / `eval` startup fast. If you only run / serve / eval / repl / test, you can skip `ramune-toolchain`.

## CLI Commands

```
ramune run [file]            Run JS/TS file (or package.json entry point)
ramune run -w file.ts        Watch mode (auto-restart on changes)
ramune run --check file.ts   Type-check then run
ramune run --sandbox file.ts Deny all permissions
ramune run --workers 4 srv.ts Multi-worker HTTP server
ramune serve <entry.ts>      Workers-style ES-module handler (export default { fetch })
ramune eval "expr"           Evaluate expression (JS/TS)
ramune test [dir]            Run test files (*.test.ts, *.spec.js)
ramune check [file|dir]      Type-check with tsgo
ramune repl                  Interactive REPL (history, completion, TS)
ramune build <file>          Bundle with esbuild
ramune compile <file>        Compile to standalone binary (go:embed)
ramune bench [dir]           Run benchmark files
ramune x <pkg>               npx-like package runner
ramune init                  Create package.json
ramune add <pkg>             Add dependency
ramune remove <pkg>          Remove dependency
ramune install               Install all dependencies
ramune setup-jit             Enable JSC JIT on macOS
ramune typegen <pkg...>      Generate .d.ts for Go packages (go: imports)
ramune skills install        Install Agent Skills for AI agents
ramune version               Show version
```

Run options: `-p <pkg>` (npm package), `-w`/`--watch`, `--check`, `--sandbox`, `--allow-read[=path]`, `--allow-write[=path]`, `--allow-net[=host]`, `--allow-env[=var]`, `--allow-run[=cmd]`.

Compile options: `-o output`, `--minify`, `--http` (Ramune.serve event loop), `--native <file.ts>` (repeatable; transpile TS to native Go extension).

Transpile options: `-o outdir`, `--module name`, `--compile` (transpile + build binary).

Typegen options: `-o output.d.ts` (default: `go.d.ts`). Accepts `go:pkg` or `pkg` syntax.

Serve options: `--port N` (default 3000), `--workers N` (independent runtimes, round-robin), `--sqlite <path>` (default `.ramune/data.db`), `--no-sqlite`, `--config <path>` (default `ramune.toml`), `--no-config`, `--secrets-prefix <p>` (default `RAMUNE_SECRET_`), `--wait-until-timeout <dur>` (default 30s, 0=forever), `--env-file`, `--sandbox`, `--allow-read/write/net/env/run`. Reads optional `ramune.toml` for `[dependencies]`, `[permissions]`, `[[kv_namespaces]]`.

## TypeScript-to-Go Transpiler (Experimental)

Ramune includes a built-in TypeScript-to-Go transpiler that converts TypeScript source code to idiomatic Go. This feature is experimental and under active development — generated code may require manual adjustments for complex codebases.

```
ramune transpile main.ts -o out/                         # single file
ramune transpile main.ts utils.ts -o out/ --module myapp # multi-file project
ramune transpile main.ts --compile -o myapp              # transpile + build binary
```

### Supported TypeScript Features

| Category | Features |
|----------|----------|
| Types | `number` → `float64`, `string`, `boolean`, `void`, `null`/`undefined` → `nil`, `any`, `unknown` → `any` |
| Collections | `T[]` → `[]T`, `Map<K,V>` → `map[K]V`, `Set<T>` → `map[T]struct{}` |
| Nullable | `T \| null`, `T \| undefined` → `*T` (pointer) |
| Generics | Functions and classes with type parameters and constraints |
| Enums | String enums → Go const block, numeric enums → iota |
| Discriminated unions | `type Shape = Circle \| Square` with narrowing via `if (s.kind === "circle")` |
| Union of literals | `"a" \| "b" \| "c"` → `string` |
| Promises | `Promise<T>` → `*promise.Promise[T]`, `async`/`await` supported |
| Classes | Fields, constructors, methods, inheritance (`extends`), static fields/methods, abstract classes, getter/setter accessors |
| Interfaces | Converted to Go struct types |
| Destructuring | Object `{a, b}` and array `[x, y]` patterns, default values (`{a = 1}`) |
| Spread | `[...arr, elem]`, `{...obj, key: val}` |
| Template literals | `` `Hello ${name}` `` → `fmt.Sprintf` |
| Operators | `typeof`, `instanceof`, `in`, `delete`, `?.` (optional chaining), `??` (nullish coalescing), `**` (exponentiation), `>>>`, `&&=`, `\|\|=`, `??=` |
| Array methods | `map`, `filter`, `reduce`, `find`, `forEach`, `includes`, `some`, `every`, `push`, `pop`, `slice`, `splice`, `concat`, `join`, etc. |
| String methods | `split`, `includes`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `trim`, `replace`, `replaceAll`, `repeat`, `padStart`, `padEnd`, etc. |
| Loops | `for`, `for...of`, `for...in`, `for await...of`, `while`, `do...while`, labeled `break`/`continue` |
| Error handling | `try`/`catch`/`finally` |
| Modules | Relative imports, Node.js built-in modules, npm packages (uuid, lodash, zod), Go packages via `go:` prefix, `export default`, re-exports |
| Go interop | `go:` prefix imports any Go package, multi-return destructuring (`const [resp, err] = fn()`), auto go.mod |
| Type resolution | Conditional types, mapped types (`Record<K,V>` → `map[K]V`), intersection types, utility types via checker |

### Type Mapping

| TypeScript | Go |
|---|---|
| `number` | `float64` |
| `string` | `string` |
| `boolean` | `bool` |
| `T[]` | `[]T` |
| `T \| null` | `*T` |
| `Map<K, V>` | `map[K]V` |
| `Set<T>` | `map[T]struct{}` |
| `Promise<T>` | `*promise.Promise[T]` |
| `any` / `unknown` | `any` |
| Enum | Named type with const block |
| Class | Struct with methods |
| Interface | Struct type |

### Transpiler Limitations

- No decorators — complex metaprogramming, not yet supported
- No generators / `yield` — Go has no generator concept; use channels or callbacks
- No dynamic `import()` — use `require()`
- No Symbol or Proxy — no Go equivalent
- Numeric precision — all numbers are `float64`
- `any`-typed property access uses `jsrt.GetField()` runtime reflection

### Go Package Imports (`go:` prefix)

Import any Go standard library or third-party package:

```typescript
import { Println, Sprintf } from "go:fmt"
import * as http from "go:net/http"
import { Default } from "go:github.com/gin-gonic/gin"

const [resp, err] = http.Get("http://example.com")  // Go multi-return
```

Generate TypeScript type definitions for type checking:

```
ramune typegen go:fmt go:net/http -o go.d.ts
```

Generates `declare module "go:fmt" { ... }` with function signatures, interfaces, constants, and type mappings (number, string, boolean, Record, tuples for multi-return, Error | null for error returns).

## Native Extension Modules

Compile TypeScript functions to native Go code callable from JS at full compiled speed:

```
ramune compile app.js --native math.ts -o myapp
ramune compile app.js --native math.ts --native geometry.ts -o myapp
```

The `--native` flag transpiles TypeScript to Go, exposing exported functions via `require('native:modulename')`.

Workflow: TypeScript → Go transpiler → Go source → NativeModuleFromFuncs → require('native:name')

Supported native function signatures:
- Primitive parameters and returns: `number`, `string`, `boolean`
- Struct parameters: JS objects auto-converted to Go structs via field name matching
- Struct returns: Go structs returned as JS objects with live getter/setter properties
- Typed slice parameters: `number[]` → `[]float64`, etc.
- Error returns: `(T, error)` — errors become JS exceptions
- Pointer returns: `*Struct` — returned with methods and mutable fields
- Panics caught and converted to JS exceptions

Not supported as native exports:
- Generic functions (must be wrapped in a non-generic function)
- Functions with channel parameters

### NativeModuleFromFuncs (Go Library API)

Create native modules from typed Go functions without manual argument parsing:

```go
mod := ramune.NativeModuleFromFuncs("native:math", map[string]any{
    "add":       func(a, b float64) float64 { return a + b },
    "fibonacci": mymath.Fibonacci,
})
rt, _ := ramune.New(ramune.NodeCompat(), ramune.WithModule(mod))
rt.Eval(`require('native:math').add(3, 4)`) // 7
```

Supports struct parameters (JS objects → Go structs), struct returns with live properties, typed slices, error handling, and panic recovery.

When a function returns a struct pointer, the JS object has live getter/setter properties and callable methods — mutations in JS are reflected in Go and vice versa.

## Go Library API

### Runtime

```go
rt, err := ramune.New(opts ...Option)

// Options
ramune.NodeCompat()              // Node.js polyfills
ramune.WithFetch()               // globalThis.fetch
ramune.Dependencies("lodash@4")  // npm packages (subpath imports supported: "react-dom/server")
ramune.PreloadJS(code)           // JS to run before dependency bundles (polyfills)
ramune.WithGC(ramune.GCConfig{}) // GC tuning
ramune.WithPermissions(perms)    // sandbox
ramune.WithModule(module)        // custom require() module

// Evaluate
val, err := rt.Eval(code)
err := rt.Exec(code)
val, err := rt.EvalAsync(code)   // resolve Promises

// Construct values
obj, _ := rt.NewObject(map[string]any{"key": "value"})
arr, _ := rt.NewArray(1, "two", true)
buf, _ := rt.NewUint8Array([]byte{0xFF})

// Go callbacks (GoFunc can safely call Value methods — no deadlock)
rt.RegisterFunc("name", func(args []any) (any, error) { ... })

// JS function arguments are wrapped as *JSFunc, callable from Go
rt.RegisterFunc("forEach", func(args []any) (any, error) {
    fn := args[0].(*ramune.JSFunc)
    defer fn.Close()
    fn.Call("hello") // invoke the JS function
    return nil, nil
})

// Typed callbacks (generics, supports *JSFunc parameters)
ramune.Register(rt, "add", func(a, b float64) float64 { return a + b })

// Struct binding
rt.Bind("user", &User{Name: "Alice", Age: 30})

// Plugin system
rt.LoadModule(ramune.Module{Name: "mydb", Exports: map[string]ramune.GoFunc{...}})

// Native module from typed functions (reflection-based, no manual arg parsing)
mod := ramune.NativeModuleFromFuncs("native:math", map[string]any{
    "add": func(a, b float64) float64 { return a + b },
})
rt, _ = ramune.New(ramune.NodeCompat(), ramune.WithModule(mod))

// Event loop
rt.Tick()
rt.RunEventLoop()
rt.Wake()   // signal event loop from any goroutine

// Multi-core pool
pool, _ := ramune.NewPool(4, ramune.NodeCompat())
pool.Eval("...")
pool.Broadcast("...")
pool.ListenAndServe(":3000", handlerJS)

rt.Close()
```

### Value

```go
val.String()                // JS string representation
val.Float64()               // as float64
val.Int64()                 // as int64
val.Bool()                  // as bool
val.Bytes()                 // TypedArray/ArrayBuffer → []byte
val.GoString()              // JS string → Go string
val.IsNull() / IsUndefined() / IsArray() / IsFunction()
val.Attr("name")            // get property
val.SetAttr("name", value)  // set property
val.Has("name")             // check property
val.Delete("name")          // delete property
val.Keys()                  // enumerate property names
val.Len()                   // length property
val.Index(i)                // array index
val.ToMap()                 // → map[string]any (via JSON)
val.ToSlice()               // → []any (via JSON)
val.Call(args...)            // call as function
val.Close()                 // release
```

### JSFunc

JS functions passed as GoFunc callback arguments are wrapped as `*JSFunc`:

```go
fn := args[0].(*ramune.JSFunc)
defer fn.Close()                    // release JS reference
result, err := fn.Call(arg1, arg2)  // invoke, returns Go value
```

### GC Configuration

```go
ramune.WithGC(ramune.GCConfig{
    GCInterval: 2000,   // manual JSC GC every N requests (default: 2000)
    GCPercent:  100,    // Go GOGC value (default: 100)
})
```

### Workers-style Modules (`github.com/i2y/ramune/workers`)

Cloudflare-Workers-style handlers — author a module that `export default { fetch, scheduled }` and serve it inside any Go HTTP server.

```go
import "github.com/i2y/ramune/workers"

// Single runtime
handler, err := workers.Register(rt, "worker.ts", src,
    workers.WithSQLite(".ramune/data.db"),    // env.DB + env.KV
    workers.WithWaitUntilTimeout(30*time.Second),
    workers.WithSecretsPrefix("APP_"),         // env.SECRETS source
)
http.ListenAndServe(":3000", handler)

// N runtimes (esbuild runs once, attached to each)
p, _ := workers.Prepare("worker.ts", src)
for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
    rt, _ := ramune.New(ramune.NodeCompat(), ramune.WithFetch())
    h, _ := workers.AttachPrepared(rt, p, workers.WithSQLite("db.db"))
    // ... wire h into a round-robin mux
}

// Pluggable backends (Redis, Postgres, in-memory ...)
// type KVBackend interface { Get/Put/Delete/List }
// type DBBackend interface { Query/Exec }  // ? placeholders
workers.Register(rt, "w.ts", src,
    workers.WithKVBackend(myRedisKV),
    workers.WithDBBackend(myPostgres),
)
```

- `ctx.waitUntil(p)` keeps the executor alive post-response until `p` settles or `WithWaitUntilTimeout` fires.
- `env.SECRETS` is a frozen map of env vars matching `WithSecretsPrefix` (default `RAMUNE_SECRET_`).
- `WithSQLite` is a convenience — `sqliteKV` / `sqliteSQLBackend` satisfy the same `KVBackend` / `DBBackend` interfaces as user-supplied backends.
- `workers.LoadRamuneTOML(path)` + `workers.ApplyRamuneTOML(toml)` parse the same `[dependencies]` / `[permissions]` / `[[kv_namespaces]]` schema the CLI uses.
- `workers.ExtractModuleConfig(rt)` inspects the default export's `route` / `cron` / `fetch` / `scheduled` fields (skips framework methods like Hono's `.route()`).
- TypeScript declarations live in `workers/workers.d.ts` (`Env`, `WorkersHandler`, `ExecutionContext`, `D1Database`, `KVNamespace`, `Secrets`, `ScheduledEvent`).
- The CLI wrapper is `ramune serve`.

### Custom `env` bindings (`workers.WithExtraEnvJS` + `RegisterFunc`)

Full extensibility story for CF Workers features Ramune does not ship (Durable Objects, Queues, R2, AI Gateway, Service Bindings, Hyperdrive). Three pieces:

1. **Go callback** — `rt.RegisterFunc("__env_foo_op", fn)` does the actual work (HTTP call, DB query, S3 put...).
2. **JS facade** — passed via `workers.WithExtraEnvJS(js)`; it mutates the env object through the `globalThis.__extraEnvBindings(env)` hook.
3. **TypeScript augmentation** (optional) — `interface Env { FOO: ... }` in a `.d.ts` merges into the built-in `Env`.

```go
// Example: env.EMAIL with a user-supplied Sender
rt.RegisterFunc("__env_email_send", func(args []any) (any, error) {
    b, _ := json.Marshal(args[0])
    var opts struct{ To, Subject, Body string }
    _ = json.Unmarshal(b, &opts)
    return nil, mailer.Send(opts.To, opts.Subject, opts.Body)
})

const facadeJS = `
globalThis.__extraEnvBindings = (function(prev) {
    return function(env) {
        if (prev) prev(env);           // compose with other bindings
        env.EMAIL = {
            send: function(opts) { return __env_email_send(opts); },
        };
    };
})(globalThis.__extraEnvBindings);
`

handler, _ := workers.Register(rt, "w.ts", src, workers.WithExtraEnvJS(facadeJS))
```

The IIFE composition around `prev` lets multiple packages stack bindings (`mailbinding.FacadeJS + queuebinding.FacadeJS + blobbinding.FacadeJS`) without collisions. `workers.WithSQLite` is a convenience built on this same pattern — it installs `KVBackend` + `DBBackend` via `WithKVBackend` / `WithDBBackend`, which both use the env-builder under the hood. See `workers/BINDINGS.md` and `examples/workers/custom-binding/` for the full walkthrough.

### Permissions

```go
ramune.WithPermissions(&ramune.Permissions{
    Read:      ramune.PermGranted,
    ReadPaths: []string{"/tmp"},
    Write:     ramune.PermDenied,
    Net:       ramune.PermDenied,
    Env:       ramune.PermGranted,
    Run:       ramune.PermDenied,
})
```

## Ramune APIs & Bun Compatibility

Ramune provides its own API namespace (`Ramune.*`). `Bun.*` is available as an alias for backward compatibility, though compatibility is partial and will be improved over time.

Supported APIs:
- `Ramune.serve({port, fetch, websocket})` — HTTP/WebSocket server (Go net/http backend, 101K req/s). Async fetch handlers with setTimeout supported.
- `Ramune.file(path)` — text(), json(), exists(), size, name
- `Ramune.write(path, data)` — file write
- `Ramune.password.hash/verify` — bcrypt
- `Ramune.sleep(ms)` — Promise-based delay
- `Ramune.hash(data)` — FNV hash
- `Ramune.plugin({setup})` — onLoad filters, virtual modules
- `Request` / `Response` — Web API polyfills (enables Hono, etc.)
- `Bun.*` — Alias for `Ramune.*` (partial Bun compatibility)
- `bun:sqlite` — pure Go SQLite (Database, Statement)

## Node.js Compatibility

Enabled via `ramune.NodeCompat()`:

| Module | Coverage | Key Functions |
|--------|----------|---------------|
| path | 100% | join, resolve, relative, normalize, isAbsolute, parse, format |

| child_process | 80% | spawnSync, execSync, execFileSync, spawn (async goroutine I/O) |
| crypto | 85% | randomBytes, randomUUID, createHash, createHmac, scryptSync, pbkdf2Sync, createCipheriv, createDecipheriv, randomInt, timingSafeEqual, createSign/Verify, generateKeyPairSync, crypto.subtle |
| stream | 85% | Readable, Writable, Transform, Duplex, PassThrough as ES6 classes (class extends supported), pipe, asyncIterator (for await...of), backpressure, cork/uncork, unshift, unpipe, objectMode, stream.pipeline, stream.finished |
| zlib | 75% | gzipSync, gunzipSync, deflateSync, inflateSync, brotliCompressSync, brotliDecompressSync |
| os | 85% | platform, arch, hostname, type, cpus, totalmem, freemem, userInfo |
| events | 85% | EventEmitter: on, once, emit, removeListener, setMaxListeners |
| http/https | 80% | http.request, http.get, http.createServer with streaming response (Go net/http backend) |
| http2 | 75% | connect, createServer, createSecureServer, trailers, multiplexing, h2c |
| net/tls | 70% | net.Socket, net.createConnection, net.createServer, tls.connect (async goroutines) |
| Buffer | 90% | from, alloc, concat, readUInt8/16/32, writeUInt8/16/32, fill, toString(hex/base64/utf8), Buffer.compare, equals, slice, copy |
| url | 80% | parse, format, resolve, fileURLToPath |
| assert | 80% | ok, strictEqual, deepStrictEqual, throws, doesNotThrow |
| util | 80% | types, promisify, callbackify, format, inspect, debuglog |
| worker_threads | 80% | Worker, parentPort, workerData, postMessage, SharedArrayBuffer, Atomics.waitAsync |

| readline | 70% | async iterator support |
| querystring | 80% | escape, unescape, stringify, parse |
| timers/promises | 70% | setTimeout, setImmediate as Promise |
| perf_hooks | basic | performance.now, mark, measure |
| process | 85% | env, cwd, platform, arch, hrtime, nextTick, exit, signals via EventEmitter, stdin/stdout/stderr with isTTY |
| tty | 70% | isatty, ReadStream, WriteStream with columns/rows |
| dgram | 70% | UDP sockets |
| async_hooks | basic | AsyncLocalStorage |
| module | — | createRequire, file-based require with ESM-to-CJS transform |
| dns | basic | lookup, resolve |

Also: TextEncoder/TextDecoder, AbortController/AbortSignal, Symbol.dispose/asyncDispose.

| `console.time` / `table` / `trace` | Supported |

## TypeScript

- `.ts`/`.tsx` files transpiled via esbuild (type annotations stripped)
- `require('./module.ts')` resolves and transpiles `.ts` files
- REPL accepts TypeScript syntax
- `ramune eval` handles TypeScript expressions
- `ramune check` uses tsgo (TypeScript 7, 10x faster than tsc)
- ESM files bundled via esbuild Build API with full import resolution

## Test Runner

```js
describe("math", () => {
    test("addition", () => {
        expect(1 + 2).toBe(3);
    });
});
```

Matchers: toBe, toEqual, toBeTruthy, toBeFalsy, toContain, toThrow, toBeGreaterThan, toBeLessThan, toHaveLength, toBeNull, toBeUndefined, toBeDefined, toHaveBeenCalledTimes, not.*.

Mocking via `jest.fn()` and `jest.spyOn()`:

```js
test("mock", () => {
    const fn = jest.fn().mockReturnValue(42);
    expect(fn()).toBe(42);
    expect(fn).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
});
```

## Architecture

- Each Runtime has a dedicated goroutine pinned to one OS thread via runtime.LockOSThread()
- All JSC operations dispatched via channel; dispatch() detects re-entrance via goroutine ID
- Independent VMs via JSContextGroupCreate + JSGlobalContextCreateInGroup (bypasses macOS shared VM)
- Channel-driven event loop with Wake() — no 10ms polling
- Multi-core via RuntimePool (N independent JSC contexts on separate OS threads)
- Map/slice conversion uses JSON.parse to avoid JSC structure table corruption from rapid C API calls
- Async handlers support setTimeout via real-time tick loop
- QuickJS backend: single-threaded interpreter via modernc.org/quickjs, pure Go, no OS thread pinning needed
- Backend selected at build time via `-tags quickjs` build tag

## Performance

### JSC backend (Apple M4 Max, JIT enabled)

| Test | Ramune | Bun | Node.js |
|------|--------|-----|---------|
| Hello World | 14.2ms | 7.1ms | 18.0ms |
| Fibonacci(35) | 46.2ms | 40.0ms | 64.7ms |
| JSON 10K | 17.6ms | 9.7ms | 22.9ms |
| Crypto SHA256 | 19.8ms | 11.0ms | 20.4ms |
| File I/O | 20.7ms | 13.3ms | 24.2ms |
| HTTP req/s (single) | 101K | 156K | 112K |
| HTTP req/s (3 workers, fib(35)) | 85 | 32 | 22 |

### QuickJS backend (same machine, no JIT)

| Test | Ramune (QuickJS) | Ramune (JSC) | Bun | Node.js |
|------|-----------------|--------------|-----|---------|
| Hello World | 19.0ms | 14.2ms | 6.4ms | 17.1ms |
| Fibonacci(35) | 3,089ms | 46.2ms | 39.3ms | 63.5ms |
| JSON 10K | 65.1ms | 17.6ms | 9.0ms | 22.0ms |
| Crypto SHA256 | 26.8ms | 19.8ms | 10.3ms | 19.5ms |
| File I/O | 25.8ms | 20.7ms | 12.4ms | 22.7ms |
| HTTP req/s (single) | 66K | 101K | 165K | 111K |

### Multi-Runtime Pool

| Workers | req/s | Scaling |
|---------|-------|---------|
| 1 | 44K | 1.0x |
| 2 | 65K | 1.48x |
| 3 | 68K | 1.56x |

### vs Go JS Runtimes

| Test | Ramune (JSC+JIT) | Ramune (QuickJS) | goja | otto |
|------|-----------------|-----------------|------|------|
| Fibonacci(35) | **31ms** | 3,122ms | 1,989ms | 26,413ms |
| JSON 10K objects | **0.9ms** | 30ms | 11ms | 27ms |

Run `make bench` to reproduce.

## Known Limitations

- **N-API / Native addons**: Not supported. Packages requiring `.node` native binaries won't work — use pure JS alternatives.
- **HTTP self-fetch**: Ramune.serve() handlers cannot fetch their own server (same JS context deadlock).
- **Windows**: JSC backend not available. Use `-tags quickjs` for Windows support.
- **Linux multi-runtime (JSC)**: On arm64, `CGO_ENABLED=1` and gcc required (cgo signal forwarding for JSC GC). On x86_64, works without cgo.
- **Multi-worker scaling (JSC)**: Scaling flattens around 4+ workers on macOS due to JSC shared-cache threading constraints.
- **QuickJS backend**: No JIT — CPU-bound JS is ~67x slower than JSC. Error stack traces not available.
- **Native module instance lifecycle**: Struct instances returned to JS are not automatically freed when JS GC collects the object. Cleaned up on Runtime.Close().
- **Generic native exports**: Generic functions cannot be exposed as native module exports; wrap in a non-generic function.

## Requirements

| | JSC backend (default) | QuickJS backend (`-tags quickjs`) |
|---|---|---|
| **Go** | 1.26+ | 1.26+ |
| **Platforms** | macOS, Linux | macOS, Linux, Windows, FreeBSD |
| **System deps** | macOS: none. Linux: `apt install libjavascriptcoregtk-4.1-dev` | None |

All tools are built in — no external dependencies needed for `check`, `fmt`, `lint`, or TypeScript transpilation. npm packages are fetched directly from the npm registry — no npm or bun CLI required.
